#### 1. muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy (congenital with intellectual disability), type B14  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:22932)

**Proposed mechanism:** GMPPB (HGNC:22932) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (GO:0006486); Glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy (HP:0003198); Glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in GMPPB disrupt the glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan, leading to congenital muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in GMPPB with a documented gain-of-function mechanism or a non-pathogenic variant with a significantly high allele frequency (>5%) in gnomAD.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of GMPPB in alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation provides a potential target for therapeutic interventions aimed at improving muscle function and cognitive outcomes in patients with these rare muscular dystroglycanopathies.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in GMPPB that result in a gain-of-function mechanism, or identification of a completely distinct causal gene for one of the diseases that does not involve the dystroglycan pathway. _(variant: Exome or genome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common variant (AF > 0.01) in GMPPB that is strongly associated with a protective effect against either disease.)_
